generatedCommentsNodes.comment: The `limit` field added to `MvExpand` is not serialized in `writeTo` and is explicitly set to `null` when read from `StreamInput`. Furthermore, the assertion `assert limit == null;` in `writeTo` will cause a crash (when assertions are enabled) if any optimized plan containing an `MvExpand` with a limit is serialized. If this field is intended only for use on the coordinator during physical mapping, it should be clearly documented why it's omitted from serialization and why the assertion exists given that the optimizer actively populates this field.

The cast `(int) limitSource.fold()` assumes that the result of `fold()` is always an `Integer`. If a `Limit` node can be constructed with a non-constant expression that cannot be folded into an integer, this will throw a `ClassCastException`. It is safer to check if the result is an instance of `Integer` before casting.

There is a logical redundancy in how limits are handled when pushed past `MvExpand`. The rule in `PushDownAndCombineLimits` transforms the plan into a structure where an `MvExpand` (with an internal limit) is the parent of a `Limit` node: `MvExpand(limit=N) -> Limit(N) -> Child`. 
When this is mapped to a physical plan in `Mapper.java`, the `Limit` node becomes a `LimitExec`, and the `MvExpand` (because it has a limit) is wrapped in another `LimitExec`. This results in two identical `LimitExec` operators wrapping the same operation: `LimitExec(N, MvExpandExec(LimitExec(N, ...)))`. Since `MvExpandExec` does not appear to use the limit internally for optimization (it's only used by the mapper to wrap it), one of these limits is redundant.

review_comment: I guess this never triggers b/c there's currently always going to be a limit below MV_EXPAND, so it'll never be serialized in the fragment, right?

It never happens because we do the serialization after the physical planning, and the mapper will resolve an `MvExpand(limit=n)` into a `LimitExec(n) + MvExpandExec`; after physical planning, even if that fragment remains the same, it will be re-translated to `Limit(n) + MvExpand` and serialized.

To clarify, we don't need to serialize it _now_, but we could. It would be yet another transport version bump, and since it's a fix and it will be backported, I preferred to make the backport as smooth as possible

I think I get it.

> To clarify, we don't need to serialize it now, but we could.

The fragment will contain the logical plan, the "original" one. So theoretically, we might need to serialise an `MvExpand` with a non-null limit. In which case the assertion would trip. But `MvExpand`'s limit would be non-`null` only if a limit was pushed down over it and since limit is a pipeline breaker, the plan will be latest broken down at the limit, so MvExpand will, in current form, never make it onto the nodes. Right?
The translation to physical and the mapping wouldn't then influence this, I guess.

> and since limit is a pipeline breaker, the plan will be latest broken down at the limit, so MvExpand will, in current form, never make it onto the nodes. Right?

Correct, and it's enough to guarantee that limited MV_EXPAND will never make it into the data nodes.

> The translation to physical and the mapping wouldn't then influence this, I guess.

I think you're right
